name: Mines Branch (Manitoba Business, Mining, Trade and Job Creation)
description: Administers The Mines and Minerals Act: prospecting licences, claim recording through the iMaQs system, mineral exploration licences, exploration work permits, mineral leases and closure plans. The department also coordinates Crown consultation on exploration authorizations.

name: Critical Minerals Office
description: Single-window office opened in April 2025 to attract investment and give mining companies customized help moving projects through permitting faster.

name: Manitoba Geological Survey
description: Publishes public geoscience (maps, field reports, the annual Report of Activities) that explorers use to choose ground. Lowers the cost and risk of early exploration.

name: Mining Advisory Council
description: Set up in 2025 with Indigenous Nations, government and industry to make recommendations on the direction of Manitoba's critical-minerals sector. Membership and influence on specific decisions not checked.
verification_note: Membership list and record of recommendations not found.

name: Manitoba Environment and Climate Change (Environmental Approvals Branch)
description: Runs assessment under The Environment Act. The Director decides Class 1 and Class 2 licences (the department lists mining as a typical Class 2 development); the Minister decides Class 3. A Technical Advisory Committee reviews proposals and comments go on a public registry. It refused Sio Silica's Vivian licence in 2024 and is now reviewing the SiMbA proposal.
projects: Sio Silica, Minago, Canadian Premium Sand, all mines
source2_title: Department presentation on classes of development (2025)

name: Clean Environment Commission
description: Arm's-length body that holds public hearings when the Minister asks, then reports advice and recommendations. It does not issue licences. Its 2023 report on Sio Silica's Vivian project found too many unanswered questions, and the province cited it when refusing the licence.
source2_title: The Narwhal on the Sio Silica decision

name: Premier and Cabinet, Government of Manitoba
description: Sets direction: the 2024 critical minerals strategy, a goal of tripling critical-mineral production in five years, and a June 2026 review of permitting rules. The Premier and Environment Minister announced the 2024 refusal of Sio Silica's licence, and in June 2026 the Premier said the province would launch a public inquiry into the company's previous actions.
source1_title: CBC: Manitoba rejects Sio Silica project
source3_title: Global News: tripling critical mineral production
source4_title: Global News: Kinew on Sio Silica MOU (June 2026)

name: The Crown in right of Manitoba (consultation function)
description: The province holds the duty to consult before decisions that may affect Aboriginal or treaty rights. For mining it works through a 2007 draft consultation policy (now an interim policy), draft procedures for exploration and mine development, and Mineral Development Protocols negotiated with individual Nations since 2019. It says it relies on proponent-led engagement.
source1_title: Procedures for Crown consultation on mineral exploration (draft)

name: Manitoba Crown-Indigenous Corporation (MCIC)
description: New Crown corporation announced in December 2025, with half its directors appointed by Manitoba and half by Indigenous Nations. It leads the Port of Churchill Plus project and aims to support Indigenous ownership in major projects. In 2025 the Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs declined to commit to an earlier version of the proposal. Its role in mining projects is still forming.
verification_note: Final legislation and board composition not confirmed; mining role prospective.
source2_title: APTN: AMC declines to commit to MCIC proposal

name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada
description: Runs federal assessment of designated projects and leads federal consultation on them. The Lynn Lake gold project received a federal decision statement in 2023 with 177 conditions; it was amended again in 2026.
source1_title: Canadian Impact Assessment Registry: Lynn Lake (80140)
source2_title: Kitco: federal approval of Lynn Lake

name: Natural Resources Canada
description: Leads federal critical-minerals policy and funds programs such as the Critical Minerals Infrastructure Fund, which gave the Manitoba Métis Federation capacity funding to engage on critical-minerals projects.
source1_title: Open Government: CMIF grant to Manitoba Métis Federation

name: Department of Finance Canada / Canada Revenue Agency
description: Writes and administers the flow-through share rules and the investor tax credits: the 15% Mineral Exploration Tax Credit and the 30% Critical Mineral Exploration Tax Credit, both available for agreements signed up to 31 March 2027.

name: Mining Board
description: Tribunal established under The Mines and Minerals Act. Its exact caseload was not checked; it is the forum the Act provides for certain disputes under the Act.
verification_note: Scope of jurisdiction described only from a legislation summary.
source1_title: FAOLEX summary of The Mines and Minerals Act

name: Manitoba Court of King's Bench
description: Hears injunctions, lawsuits and judicial reviews. In 2013 (as Queen's Bench) it granted Hudbay an injunction against blockades by Mathias Colomb Cree Nation; in 2023 the Nation sued Manitoba and Manitoba Hydro here over the Laurie River dams.
source2_title: CBC: Mathias Colomb sues over Laurie River dams

name: Supreme Court of Canada
description: Defined the Crown's duty to consult (Haida Nation, 2004). In May 2026 it granted British Columbia leave to appeal Gitxaała, in which BC's Court of Appeal found BC's former free-entry claim system inconsistent with UNDRIP. The ruling will not bind Manitoba's statute directly but will shape the debate over free entry everywhere.
source2_title: MLT Aikins on the 2023 trial decision and Haida

name: Norway House Cree Nation (Kinosao Sipi)
description: Treaty 5 Nation of about 8,700 members. It bought 100% of the Minago nickel project from Flying Nickel for $8 million in 2024, after earlier signing an impact and benefit agreement with that company. In March 2026 Manitoba amended Minago's licence; the first phase is magnesium from surface dolomite. Both rights holder and project owner.
source1_title: CIM Magazine: Norway House acquires Minago

name: Marcel Colomb First Nation
description: Nation at Lynn Lake. Signed a 2023 agreement with Alamos Gold covering revenue sharing, jobs and training. Its chief called the 2025 groundbreaking the first time the Nation had been involved in a mining project on its lands.
source1_title: BNN / Canadian Press: construction begins at Lynn Lake

name: Mathias Colomb Cree Nation (Pukatawagan)
description: Nation whose asserted traditional territory includes the Lynn Lake and Snow Lake areas. It issued stop-work orders and blockaded Hudbay's Lalor site in 2013, appealed provincial licences for Lynn Lake, then signed an impact benefit agreement with Alamos in 2025 and withdrew the appeals. It is suing Manitoba and Manitoba Hydro over dams. Positions vary by project and over time.
source2_title: CBC: Hudbay sues First Nation over blockade (2013)

name: Kiciwapa Cree Nation
description: Woodland Cree Nation based in Sherridon that asserts Treaty 6 adhesion rights. Since 2022 it has signed exploration agreements with T2 Metals, Kinross Gold, Foremost Clean Energy and Boreal Gold, covering notice, monitoring, jobs and contributions to a community fund. PrairiesCan funds its engagement and exploration growth plan.
verification_note: Formal status (for example whether it is a band under the Indian Act) not confirmed; descriptions come from company releases and federal grant records.

name: Hollow Water First Nation (Wanipigow)
description: Anishinaabe Treaty 5 Nation on the east side of Lake Winnipeg. Partner, with Seymourville, in Canadian Premium Sand's Participation Agreement; 1911 Gold's True North mine sits in its traditional territory. Camp Morning Star, on the Nation's land, opposes silica sand mining, so views within the community differ.
source1_title: Canadian Premium Sand: Selkirk site and partners

name: Sagkeeng First Nation
description: Nation whose ancestral lands include the Bird River belt in southeastern Manitoba. Has an exploration agreement with Grid Metals and supported its advanced exploration permit for the Donner lithium project.
projects: Donner Lake, Falcon West, Makwa-Mayville (Grid Metals)
source1_title: The Assay: Grid Metals AEP update

name: Brokenhead Ojibway Nation
description: The First Nation closest to Sio Silica's proposed wells. In 2020 it asked for a joint federal–provincial review. In August 2025 members voted down a partnership offering 5% of profits. Leadership has said MOUs on the project were signed without its consent and that water protection comes first.

name: Long Plain First Nation
description: Signed an MOU with Sio Silica to lead an Indigenous-led environmental review of the project, combining Western science and traditional knowledge, with the right to suspend or end its participation.
source1_title: Canadian Mining Journal: Indigenous community leads review
source2_title: Sio Silica: Long Plain to lead review

name: Nisichawayasihk Cree Nation
description: Nation near Thompson. Joined the City of Thompson and the steelworkers' union in a 2024 lobby in Ottawa for the future of the Thompson operations, and hosted a northern mining workshop at the UCN Linkages conference.
verification_note: No agreement with the Thompson operator was found.
source2_title: UCN Linkages: NCN Northern Mining Workshop

name: Manitoba Métis Federation (Red River Métis)
description: Government of the Red River Métis. Asserts consultation rights on mining files (Tanco, Lynn Lake, Hudbay) and is drafting a Red River Métis Mineral Development Protocol. Listed among Indigenous groups in the Lynn Lake federal decision statement and consulted on the Minago licence. Signed an MOU with the Southern Chiefs' Organization on the Crown-Indigenous Corporation.

name: Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs
description: Province-wide political organization of First Nations. In August 2025 its chiefs declined to commit to the province's Crown-Indigenous Corporation proposal, objecting that First Nations would hold only 5 of 12 seats. Promotes First Nations participation in critical-minerals trade.

name: Manitoba Keewatinowi Okimakanak (MKO)
description: Organization of northern Manitoba First Nations. Calls for free, prior and informed consent and asked the province, the Canada Infrastructure Bank and the Manitoba Chambers of Commerce to co-develop a framework with First Nations for a northern critical-minerals infrastructure study (November 2025).
source1_title: MKO response to Mineral Development Fund announcement
source2_title: CBC: MKO grand chief on resource projects

name: Southern Chiefs' Organization
description: Represents 34 southern Manitoba First Nations, including Brokenhead. In January 2026 it criticized Manitoba for signing a western critical-minerals MOU without first consulting First Nations.

name: Minago Development GP Inc.
description: Norway House-owned company advancing the Minago project: a low-emission magnesium plant first, using surface dolomite, with nickel and platinum-group metals later. The province gave $2 million toward the first phase in 2026; final planning and financing are still needed.

name: Hudbay Minerals
description: Manitoba's longest-running miner. Its Snow Lake operations include the Lalor gold-copper-zinc mine, the New Britannia and Stall mills and the 1901 deposit; a September 2026 plan extends reserve life to 18 years. It closed the Flin Flon 777 mine and zinc plant in 2022. Its relationship with Mathias Colomb Cree Nation has been contested.
projects: Lalor, 1901, Snow Lake; Flin Flon closure
source1_title: Hudbay Snow Lake mine plan (28 Sept 2026)

name: Vale Base Metals
description: Operated Thompson (inherited from Inco) until selling it to Exiro Nickel; the sale closed in October 2026. Vale keeps an 18.9% stake, offtake rights to the nickel concentrate for at least five years, and up to $200 million in price-linked payments.

name: Exiro Nickel Company
description: New owner and operator of the Thompson Operations: two underground mines, a mill and exploration ground along the 135-km Thompson Nickel Belt. Backed by Exiro Minerals, Orion Resource Partners and the Canada Growth Fund with up to US$200 million; CEO Shastri Ramnath grew up in Manitoba.
source1_title: Mining.com: Vale to sell Manitoba nickel complex

name: Alamos Gold
description: Building the Lynn Lake gold project: construction decision January 2025, delayed by the 2025 wildfires, first gold expected in the first half of 2029, initial capital now $937 million. Has impact benefit agreements with both nearby Nations.
projects: Lynn Lake (Gordon, MacLellan, Burnt Timber, Linkwood)

name: Tanco mine (Sinomine Resource Group)
description: Underground mine at Bernic Lake operated since 1969, owned since 2019 by China's Sinomine through Tantalum Mining Corporation of Canada. Produces cesium, lithium spodumene concentrate and tantalum, and has announced a large expansion including open-pit mining. About 150 workers, mostly from southeastern Manitoba (2022 figure).
verification_note: Status of the expansion and its timeline (target cited as September 2026) not confirmed from a primary source.

name: Kinross Gold
description: Global gold producer exploring in northwest Manitoba under a June 2025 exploration agreement with Kiciwapa Cree Nation, which includes letters of support for permits.
source1_title: Kinross: agreement with Kiciwapa Cree Nation

name: McEwen Inc.
description: Acquired Canadian Gold Corp. in January 2026 to get the Tartan mine near Flin Flon, a past producer (1987–89). A March 2026 resource estimate supports a planned restart.

name: 1911 Gold
description: Owns the True North mine and mill at Bissett in the Rice Lake belt, within Hollow Water First Nation's traditional territory. A 2026 economic study supports an underground restart, targeted for 2027. Also listed on the TSX Venture.

name: Sio Silica
description: Proposes extracting high-purity silica sand through wells in the RM of Springfield. The Vivian proposal was refused in February 2024 after a CEC hearing. A revised SiMbA proposal, seeking a licence for years 0–4 only, was filed in October 2025 and is under review. In June 2026 it announced offtake MOUs with RCT Solutions and NanoXSolar and a shipping arrangement through Churchill.

name: Canadian Premium Sand
description: Holds the Wanipigow silica sand quarry leases near Hollow Water First Nation and plans a solar-glass plant in Selkirk. Its licence was approved in February 2024, two days before Sio Silica's was refused. Federal and provincial governments said they intend to provide up to $272 million.
projects: Wanipigow quarry, Selkirk solar glass plant
verification_note: Current construction and financing status not confirmed.
source2_title: Up to $272M in government support (Canadian Press)

name: Grid Metals
description: TSX Venture junior with the Donner Lake lithium project (75% Grid, 25% Lithium Royalty Corp.), the Falcon West lithium-cesium project east of Winnipeg, and the Makwa-Mayville nickel-copper project, all on Sagkeeng ancestral lands. Has an MOU to process ore at Tanco. In 2023 the Wilderness Committee reported its claims inside a Nopiming Park backcountry zone.

name: T2 Metals
description: TSX Venture junior exploring the Sherridon copper-zinc-gold project. Its exploration agreements with Kiciwapa Cree Nation (2022) and with Kiciwapa and Mathias Colomb (2023) include a reserve fund drawn from exploration spending. In October 2026 it added Kiciwapa Headman Floyd North to its advisory board.
source2_title: T2 Metals and KCN recognized at MPDA gala

name: Boreal Gold
description: CSE-listed junior exploring in northwest Manitoba and northeast Saskatchewan. Signed an exploration agreement with Kiciwapa Cree Nation in March 2026.

name: Foremost Clean Energy
description: Uranium and lithium explorer (NASDAQ, CSE) with lithium properties near Snow Lake. Received a $300,000 Mineral Development Fund grant in 2021 and signed an exploration agreement with Kiciwapa Cree Nation in February 2026.
source2_title: Northern Miner: Manitoba juniors and lithium

name: Independent prospectors
description: Anyone with a prospecting licence can stake any number of claims (16 to 256 ha each) on open Crown mineral land, by posts in unsurveyed territory, then record them through iMaQs. Prospectors often option claims to juniors. Generic node: no individual is named.

name: Mining Association of Manitoba (MAMI)
description: Speaks for mining producers. Backs the critical minerals strategy and the single-desk Critical Minerals Office, arguing that permitting delays cost money.
source1_title: Canadian Press via Pique: speedier approvals

name: Manitoba Prospectors and Developers Association (MPDA)
description: Founded 1982; speaks for explorers. Pushes for modernizing The Mines and Minerals Act, including online map staking, and hosts an annual Mineral Sector Indigenous Reconciliation Gala.

name: Prospectors & Developers Association of Canada (PDAC)
description: National explorers' association. Lobbies to keep flow-through tax credits and runs the March convention in Toronto where Manitoba announces funding.

name: Quesnel Brothers Drilling
description: Drilling contractor on T2 Metals' Sherridon program, which employed and trained Kiciwapa members.

name: EarthEx Geophysics
description: Geophysics firm present at the Kinross–Kiciwapa agreement signing. Its contract role was not confirmed.
verification_note: Only its attendance at the signing is documented.

name: TSX, TSX Venture and CSE exchanges
description: Where most Manitoba juniors list and raise equity. Flow-through financings provide about 70% of the money raised on Canadian exchanges for exploration.

name: Flow-through investors and funds
description: Individuals and limited partnerships that buy flow-through shares to deduct exploration spending, plus the 15% or 30% federal credit and, for Manitoba residents, Manitoba's 30% credit. Generic node.
source1_title: Finance Canada backgrounder on the METC

name: Manitoba Mineral Development Fund (MMDF)
description: Provincial fund delivered by the Manitoba Chambers of Commerce since 2019. Grants support exploration, supply-chain and Indigenous partnership projects; in March 2026 it backed Minago and eight exploration projects.

name: Manitoba Finance (Mineral Exploration Tax Credit)
description: Administers Manitoba's 30% non-refundable tax credit for residents who buy flow-through shares funding exploration in Manitoba. Made permanent in the 2023 budget.

name: Canada Growth Fund
description: Federally owned investment fund; a cornerstone investor in Exiro Nickel's purchase of Thompson.
source1_title: Mining.com: Vale to sell Manitoba nickel complex

name: PrairiesCan
description: Federal regional development agency. Its Strategic Partnerships Initiative funds Kiciwapa Cree Nation's engagement and exploration growth plan (agreement value $515,610, 2024–2026).

name: Canada Infrastructure Bank
description: Named by MKO as a party to a feasibility study of northern infrastructure needed for critical-minerals development. Its exact funding role was not confirmed.
verification_note: Role known only from MKO's statement.

name: Orion Resource Partners
description: Mining investment firm; cornerstone investor with the Canada Growth Fund in Exiro Nickel.

name: Lithium Royalty Corp.
description: Holds 25% of the Donner Lake lithium joint venture with Grid Metals.

name: Elemental Royalty
description: Lists a 2% net smelter return royalty on the Tartan Lake gold project, operated by McEwen.

name: Nations Royalty Corp.
description: Majority Nisga'a-owned royalty company on the TSX Venture since 2024. It pools royalties that First Nations hold under benefit agreements and invites Nations across Canada to join as shareholders. Also an Indigenous-owned enterprise.
verification_note: No Manitoba royalty or partnership found; included because it is a model Manitoba Nations are being offered.
source1_title: CBC: Nations Royalty and the Nisga'a Nation
source2_title: Nations Royalty appoints VP Corporate Development

name: City of Thompson
description: Built around nickel since the 1956 discovery. Its mayor welcomed Exiro's purchase and planned investment; the city lobbied Ottawa with the union and Nisichawayasihk Cree Nation in 2024.

name: Town of Lynn Lake
description: Former mining town more than 1,000 km north of Winnipeg; host town for Alamos's Lynn Lake project.
source1_title: BNN / Canadian Press: Lynn Lake groundbreaking

name: Town of Snow Lake
description: Host town for Hudbay's Lalor mine; Hudbay has invested in the airport and new residential lots.

name: City of Flin Flon
description: Mining city on the Saskatchewan border. Lost its mine and zinc plant in 2022; McEwen's Tartan restart is 12 km away.
source1_title: Western Investor: Flin Flon's only mine shutting down

name: RM of Springfield
description: Rural municipality east of Winnipeg where Sio Silica proposes its wells. Council raised water concerns during the first review; the mayor now says he will defer to the province. Two councillors helped organize a private referendum on the project.

name: City of Selkirk
description: Proposed site of Canadian Premium Sand's solar-glass plant, expected to employ about 250 people; its mayor has called the project transformational.

name: Lac du Bonnet
description: Community nearest the Tanco mine; its mayor supports critical-minerals development without environmental damage.

name: Wilderness Committee
description: Campaigns to end mining and claim staking in provincial parks; counted 681 claims inside Manitoba parks in early 2024 and reported claims staked in a Nopiming backcountry zone. Runs letter-writing tools on Sio Silica.
source1_title: Global News: mining claims in parks
source2_title: Wilderness Committee: end mining in parks

name: Manitoba Eco-Network
description: Intervened in the Sio Silica CEC hearing with Our Line in the Sand, hiring independent experts, and filed comments asking the province to reject the SiMbA proposal or designate it Class 3.

name: MiningWatch Canada
description: National watchdog; has written on Manitoba's claim-staking system and circulates Manitoba campaigns.
source1_title: MiningWatch: Staking a claim in Manitoba

name: Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives – Manitoba
description: Policy think tank that has published analysis arguing the Sio Silica proposal should be a Class 3 development and questioning Canadian Premium Sand's technical claims.

name: Our Line in the Sand
description: Residents' group formed in 2020 after landowners were told they could not subdivide because of mineral claims beneath their land. Intervened at the CEC and opposes Sio Silica's revised proposal; chair Tangi Bell.

name: Camp Morning Star
description: Camp on Hollow Water First Nation, established in February 2019 to oppose silica sand mining. Sources differ on whether it targets Canadian Premium Sand's quarry, Sio Silica, or both.
verification_note: Which projects it targets is described differently across sources.
source1_title: APTN on Brokenhead vote and the camp

name: Manitoba Energy Justice Coalition
description: Volunteer coalition working to stop silica sand mining in Manitoba; co-launched the Save Our Water campaign.

name: United Steelworkers Local 6166
description: Union for workers at the Thompson operations. Lobbied Ottawa with the city and Nisichawayasihk Cree Nation in 2024 and has criticized past under-investment.

name: Manitoba Chambers of Commerce
description: Province-wide business federation. Delivers the Mineral Development Fund for the province and promotes Manitoba mining at PDAC.

name: InterGroup Consultants
description: Winnipeg consulting firm with about 50 years of work in regulatory affairs, environmental management and public policy for utilities, governments, regulators and Indigenous communities, including in mining. No public record tying it to a specific current Manitoba mine was found, so no links are drawn.
verification_note: Specific mining clients and files not publicly confirmed.
source1_title: InterGroup job posting describing the firm

name: Apiichitaa Inc.
description: Company with offices in Winnipeg and Campbell River, BC, associated with Linda Murphy, an Indigenous geoscientist. It was the contact for the NCN Northern Mining Workshop at UCN's Linkages conference. Its services and clients were not confirmed.
verification_note: Role inferred from a conference listing and a professional profile.
source1_title: UCN Linkages: NCN Northern Mining Workshop

name: AECOM
description: Engineering and environmental consultancy that prepared Sio Silica's 2021 Environment Act Proposal and appears on the SiMbA filings.

name: AMC Mining Consultants
description: Prepared the 2026 preliminary economic assessment for 1911 Gold's True North restart.
source1_title: Canadian Mining Journal: 1911 Gold commences PEA

name: Shared Pathway Solutions
description: Present at the Kinross–Kiciwapa signing ceremony. Its role was not confirmed.

name: Public Interest Law Centre (Legal Aid Manitoba)
description: Represented the Manitoba Eco-Network and Our Line in the Sand at the Sio Silica CEC hearing.

name: University of Manitoba
description: Research on consent and mining (Natural Resources Institute), mineral geology, and resource business (Asper School). Shapes how the issues are framed rather than any single decision; no links drawn.
source1_title: Sadiq & Sinclair on FPIC in mining (CIM Journal)

name: University College of the North
description: Northern college whose annual Linkages conference in Thompson hosts mining workshops, including Alamos and Nisichawayasihk sessions.

name: Sinomine Resource Group (parent; lithium chemical plants in China)
description: Sinomine's lithium-salt plants in Jiangxi; Tanco's first spodumene concentrate shipments went to China for Sinomine's own processing.

name: RCT Solutions GmbH
description: German solar manufacturer; signed an MOU in June 2026 for potential offtake of Sio Silica's high-purity silica and to explore a solar manufacturing hub in Canada.

name: NanoXSolar
description: US company; signed an MOU in June 2026 for potential offtake of Sio Silica's silica.

name: Solar module makers (Qcells, Heliene, Meyer Burger)
description: Signed offtake agreements in 2022–2023 for Canadian Premium Sand's planned solar glass. Whether these agreements are still in force was not checked.
verification_note: Current status of the 2023 offtake agreements not confirmed.

name: Gold refiners and bullion buyers
description: Buy doré and concentrate from Manitoba gold mines. Generic node: specific refiners not identified.
projects: Lalor; later Lynn Lake, Tartan, True North

name: Manitoba Hydro
description: Provincial Crown utility. Low-carbon, low-cost power is a selling point for Manitoba mining, but Hydro has warned since 2023 that it lacks spare capacity for new energy-intensive customers; the Premier has disputed this. Also a defendant in Mathias Colomb's dam lawsuit. A government body placed here for its infrastructure role.
source1_title: CBC: Hydro can't serve new energy-intensive customers
source2_title: CBC: Premier says Hydro has megawatts

name: Arctic Gateway Group (Port of Churchill)
description: Operates the Port of Churchill. Partner with the Crown-Indigenous Corporation on Churchill Plus and party to Sio Silica's June 2026 MOU, which foresees silica shipped to Germany through Churchill.
